features.title: One workspace for the whole week.
features.description: Everything a small team needs to agree on the work, do it, and look back honestly.

tasks.title: Table, board, timeline and graph.
tasks.description: Edit inline, group by section or person, drag cards, undo mistakes. The same tasks in four views.

planning.title: An honest picture of the week.
planning.description: Set weekly plans, record the work that happened and compare the two. Copy last week into the next one in a click.

timeoff.title: Absences that understand capacity.
timeoff.description: Vacation and flexible days with accruals, approvals and a team calendar that shows who is away on the timeline.

dependencies.title: See what comes before what.
dependencies.description: Link tasks across projects, spot unfinished predecessors and carry unfinished work into next week without double counting.

inbox.title: Know when something needs you.
inbox.description: Assignments, comments, @mentions and time-off decisions land in one inbox, with a badge for what is new.

api.title: Automate it, or ask an assistant.
api.description: Personal access tokens, a REST API and an MCP server let scripts, Claude or Codex create and update tasks with your permissions.

how.title: From a task to a clearer week.

one.title: Lay out the work.
one.description: Create a project, add tasks and make ownership clear. Import from Asana if you are moving over.

two.title: Make room for the week.
two.description: Choose commitments for the period, with time off in the same context.

three.title: Keep the picture honest.
three.description: Record work, review plan against fact, then copy the week and carry over what is unfinished.

items.one: Plan and fact live next to each other, not in separate spreadsheets.
items.two: Time off and capacity are built in, not bolted on.
items.three: A fast table with inline editing, keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl/Cmd+K) and Undo.
items.four: Start in minutes: sign in with Google, or import a project from Asana.
items.five: An open API and MCP server, with tokens limited to what you can do.
items.six: Weekly rhythm tools: copy last week, defaults for new tasks, carry over unfinished work.

cons.title: Where it is not for you (yet)

items.one: The workspace interface is English only; this website is available in six languages.
items.two: It is a web app: no native mobile apps (the browser works, wide tables scroll sideways).
items.three: No private projects: everyone in a workspace sees all of its tasks.
items.five: Notifications live in the in-app Inbox; there are no e-mail digests yet.
items.seven: Recurring tasks are not supported yet.
items.eight: It is a young product: expect rough edges and quick changes.

one.a: Yes. Choose Try for free, sign in and you get an empty workspace to explore. No payment details are asked. Plans and pricing have not been announced.

two.a: With your Google account. The first sign-in creates your account and your own workspace, so signing up and signing in are the same step.

three.q: Can I bring my work from Asana?
three.a: Yes. Export a project from Asana and import it from the Projects page; sections, assignees, dates, tags and dependencies come along.

four.a: People you invite to your workspace. Inside a workspace every member can see all tasks; roles decide who can edit, manage people and approve time off.

five.a: Yes: a REST API and an MCP server, authorised with personal access tokens that never exceed your own permissions. See the API and MCP docs.

six.q: Can my team use it together?
six.a: Yes. Invite teammates with a link and give them a role: owner, admin, member or viewer.
